title: Notes of Ministry - 30 - May 1975

paragraphs.text: The Lord would give us, beloved, a very real sense of His own personal movements in relation to the home-going of our beloved sister. As we have been reminded in prayer, He has gone down into His garden. He has gathered one of the lilies; He has gathered our beloved sister to Himself. We do not think of our sister as cut off; the Messiah was cut off and had nothing (see Daniel 9: 26). We think of our beloved sister as tenderly and carefully gathered as a lily, ready to be gathered. There is a glory about each star, as we have been reminded, and there is a glory about each lily, and the Lord has valued our sister and has gathered her. It is always important to discern what the Lord is doing, and even more important to seek to discern what He has in mind in what He does.

We think of Christ, with our affections stirring towards Him, as the One of whom we can say, “My beloved”. He has gone down into His garden; this is a matter which affects us all. It has taken place in this locality, but it is intended to affect us all because the Lord would bring about body feelings in every one of these occasions when He moves in this way. Our beloved brother is peculiarly feeling the sorrow of it, but we are all feeling it with him, all the members are feeling it with him. And if we can think of our beloved sister as glorified because she has gone into a realm of glory, all the members rejoice. So body feelings would enter into this, because when it speaks of “his garden”, the Lord would be saying, ‘My assembly’.

But then it says, He has “gone down ... to the beds of spices”. I think that is one of the ways in which the Lord would touch our affections afresh. The “beds of spices” are needed for the holy anointing oil, one of the primary elements in the holy anointing oil being liquid myrrh.

The Lord’s own suffering love would affect our hearts at this time. He has not moved without care and deliberation, the Lord never does. The Lord knew the grief that would come into our hearts in this matter, but it is intended to bring about with us a fresh impression of the suffering love of the glorious Man who went into death and has come out of it triumphant.

What a victory indeed there is as we think of the Lord out of death and moving in an area which belongs to Him. “The beds of spices” would have in view the anointing of the whole glorious system so that there is more for God, more fragrance for the Father and the Lord and the Spirit out of this very matter.

So it says He has gone down “to feed in the gardens”. We sometimes put things the other way round; we look for food from the Lord. But the Spirit would have been carefully over Solomon as he wrote this, “to feed in the gardens”. Is that what the Lord is finding as He comes into the local assemblies? This is not exactly ‘my garden’, it is “the gardens”. This has in view every locality where there are persons who are seeking to move in the light of the assembly, and as the Lord comes in He looks for food. Are we giving Him that? Is there going to be more for Him from this locality as a result of this matter? Is He going to draw all of us more into this great spiritual area of things where He is moving?

None of us would want to bring the Lord back into flesh and blood; He has been in flesh and blood in perfection of humanity; but now He is in a glorious spiritual sphere. When He moves in this way I believe it is particularly to draw our hearts and lives and minds more and more into the realm where He is, where death and sin and sorrow never have entrance. As He comes into His local assemblies He looks for us to be in the gain of this glorious victory; so He looks for food. He came into one of His gardens, according to Luke 24, and there was a little trouble there at the time. But the word from the Lord soon brought in peace and His inquiry was, “Have ye anything here to eat?” (Luke 24: 41). Is the Lord going to secure more? Our beloved sister was ready to be taken, and I think the Lord would have discerned that our beloved brother was ready for this fresh spiritual test, that he might have some fresh experience of the comfort of divine Persons so that by way of even deeper experience than he has had before he might be able to comfort the brethren. Then all of us are to get some gain from the Lord’s movements in this way and to see that there is more by way of food for the Lord as he comes in. “Part of a broiled fish and of a honeycomb” was what they had on that occasion in Luke 24, and the Lord looks for something fresh as He comes in. He comes in “to feed in the gardens and to gather lilies”. We are all going to be gathered very soon, as our hymn (No. 140) reminded us. Our beloved sister has been gathered now, but we are all going to be gathered very soon; the waiting time is a test as to whether we are going to provide more for the Lord as the fruit of His own movements in patient love at this present time.

And then this brings out a fresh movement in our hearts towards Christ. How we delight to say, “I am my beloved’s”. What a comfort it is to be conscious that we belong to Christ, and then we can say too, “My beloved is mind”. Then He Himself brings in the food, “He feedeth his flock among the lilies”. What a glorious area we are brought into in the assembly! The assembly belongs to Christ; it is His assembly, and from it He has the right to call one as He will and He has the right to move as He will in His own sphere. May our hearts be encouraged, beloved, to be more drawn out to Christ in the sphere which is living to Him and, under Him, living to God, so may we provide more for Him at the present time until He takes us all to be with Himself in glory for ever, for His name’s sake.
Word given at the burial of our beloved sister Mrs. T. Broughton, Richmond

In the readings we have had there has been an appeal to persons who would be expected to continue the testimony, if the Lord does not come for us soon. In this second chapter of John’s first epistle he addresses the saints as his own children, not exactly as children of God, which chapter 3 presents. He begins the chapter by saying, “My children”, and he continues the subject of his family in verse 12, “I write to you, children”, that is, all who belong to his family. There are three stages of growth in that family—the fathers, the young men, and the little children. John has a right, because of his apostleship, to take the place of being a father and having children. In a sense they are the children of the testimony. To apply it to our own day, without going too far, it would be like the children of the ministry of the revival. There are those who have gone before us who have taught, based on what is in the Scriptures, and on what was set up from the beginning, and we are meant to be persons who are thus instructed. We were speaking of the teaching and fellowship of the apostles, Acts 2: 42. Not only did they listen to the teaching of the apostles, but they had their fellowship, their practical fellowship. Any one of the apostles would be approachable about any matter of soul history that anyone might have, or any individual difficulty. So we are meant to be of the family of the testimony which has been brought to bear upon us in the revival.
The young men of John’s family represent the intermediate stage of growth. There has been an appeal to young men in these meetings, and this scripture would apply, of course, to them.

But it would apply to more than literal young men, because the next stage which John refers to is the fathers. John has no instruction, and no exhortation, to give to the fathers, because they had reached stability. They “have known him that is from the beginning”. I do not know how many of us would take the place of being fathers in this sense, therefore the idea of young men might be more embracing than just literal young men. “I have written to you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one”.

Reference has been made to energy. We need to apply our energies in a right direction. How important this is! The little children are in danger of the attacks of the wicked one by false teaching, and that kind of thing. Now the unction, which John points out later in this chapter, would protect them, and keep them right as they are true to it.

The young men have overcome the wicked one. There has been a certain development and growth. They know what is right and what is wrong, “Because ye are strong, and the word of God abides in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one”. The word is, “Love not the world, nor the things in the world”. If there is to be further growth, and formation, we need to protect ourselves from being diverted by the world and the things of the world. This would not only apply to younger persons, but to all of us, because we can all be diverted, unless we have “known him that is from the beginning”, which would be fulness of growth in John’s family. Such were at a stage where John addresses them as fathers, “Ye have known him that is from the beginning”. There is a certain stability reached, but I do not know how many of us would have reached that. Therefore this intermediate stage is so important, that we should persevere. “They persevered in the teaching and fellowship of the apostles, in breaking of bread and prayers”, Acts 2: 42. John continues, “Love not the world, nor the things in the world. If any one love the world, the love of the Father is not in him; because all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father but is of the world”. How near these things are to us! We do not need to take a journey to come under the influence of these things. They are in every one of us, in the flesh in us. The safeguard is the love of the Father.
Now I would like to refer to three young men in the Old Testament who would be examples for us. They had come to an intermediate stage of growth, and they go on to become fathers.

The first is Joseph who at seventeen years of age was feeding the flock with his brethren. He had found a circle of interest according to the will of God, according to what the Lord would have him do. He had found sufficient scope for his energies. He was strong, he was feeding the flock with his brethren. He had overcome the wicked one. He had no fellowship with the evil discourse of his brethren, who had the same father. He had overcome the wicked one. He had a judgment and could confide in his father Jacob as to his judgment of the evil discourse of his brethren. He kept himself, and he was loved by his father. “If any one love the world, the love of the Father is not in him”. Joseph had the love of his father in him. He found this circle of interests and he was in the enjoyment of the love of his father. What a protective circle this is! What salvation it was for Joseph to find an environment in which he could breathe freely! In the strength of the love of his father, he went through the sufferings which his brethren subjected him to, being sold into Egypt. He had thirteen years of suffering in Egypt. What sustained him? It was on the one hand the enjoyment of his father’s love, and on the other hand the light imparted to him by God in the dreams he had. See what a privileged area this is to be in, to find in the christian circle a circle of interests to which we can direct our energies and apply ourselves.

The next one I would speak about is David. He began as a young man. He fed his father’s flock at Bethlehem. He overcame the wicked one. As a very young man he slew the lion and the bear. He knew what it was to overcome. He knew what it was to be in victory, according to his measure. We might never have known that, because it was his own secret history, had it not been that Saul tried to dissuade him from meeting Goliath. David tells him the secret, that he knew a better armour than Saul’s; he had proved it. He had devoted his energies to feeding his father’s sheep at Bethlehem. It would be like the local company; we are to devote our energies to promoting the Lord’s interests in the places in which we are. We find that Saul sends for him to come into his court and play with the harp to remove the evil spirit, but David went back to feed his father’s flock at Bethlehem. He knew what it was to find locally a circle of interests for his energies, to which he committed himself. He found salvation and he was able to grow according to God in that environment. Also, David got light early as to the ark, which would be Christ typically.

The third one is Daniel, who was also young. He had light as to Jerusalem, and although he was carried captive and put in very trying circumstances, he was able to overcome the wicked one. He reached this intermediate stage of growth that John would, refer to as his young men, and he goes on to fatherhood. He becomes an old man, and what a father he became among the captives! He prayed, and what light God was able to impart to Daniel! He as a young man refused the king’s delicate food, and the wine which he drank, which would be so attractive to youth. Not only did he refuse the king’s delicate food and the wine that he drank, but he told the man who was set over them what to give them. He said, ‘Give us pulse and water’, which would be most unattractive to the natural mind. He developed a taste for the truth, for the Scriptures, for accredited ministry. He preferred it. Think of that!—He preferred it! He chose it, rather than what was so attractive to the flesh. “Love not the world, nor the things in the world”; that was Daniel. He became an overcomer.

These young men in the Old Testament would encourage us to commit ourselves, encourage us to persevere, to go on to full growth. We were reminded in Edinburgh recently that the divine objective for us all is full growth, “until we all arrive ... at the full-grown man, at the measure of the stature of the fulness of the Christ”, Ephesians 4: 13. That calls for perseverance. May the Lord encourage us, so that this work of formation may go on with every one of us. It means that we commit ourselves and persevere, the Spirit helping us. May it be so for His name’s sake.

articles.title: ACCORDING TO THE DUE ORDER
articles.author: H. C. Midgley
articles.place: Word in meeting for ministry, Brooklyn, N.Y.

paragraphs.text: I was impressed by the expression of our brother in his prayer, that God can be hindered in no thought of His. We can see, in the first portion of the verses read how David failed; he resorted to a Philistine means of bringing up the ark. It was a new cart; it was not a suitable substitute for the shoulders of the Levites. It was contrary to the divine command and Jehovah could not prosper it. Indeed, it led to disaster. David was not shining at his best in this issue. It says, “David was indignant, because Jehovah had made a breach upon Uzzah … And David was afraid of Jehovah that day”. We think of David, a man of God, having history with God behind him—and what a history! He had proved God. But the incident brings out the importance of having constant links with divine Persons. We cannot be careless or indifferent, even for a moment, for the enemy is always ready to take advantage. David unwittingly slipped into the use of this Philistine device and he lost the sense of Jehovah’s favour; he was “afraid of Jehovah that day”. One would desire that we take home to ourselves the need for constant, uninterrupted communion. Precious ministry has been before us of late, calling attention to the necessity for the use of the water of purification for cleansing in order to have constant communion. We need to avail ourselves of it lest we be defiled and hindered in communion and in our intimate links with divine Persons.
We see in David how a man recovers himself quickly, and we all can take courage as we see it. God is not hindered in any thought of His; He is going through with what He has in mind.

If you or I fail God, He has others. He has His reserves. The house of Obed-Edom was available to care for the ark. When David heard that Jehovah had blessed the house of Obed-Edom, he recovered himself quickly. I think that is delightful, “It was told king David, saying, Jehovah has blessed the house of Obed-Edom, and all that is his, because of the ark of God”. So David’s exercises are set in motion. Who can tell the extent of what he went through in those days? But he recovered himself quickly. I commend this to us. We need to walk soberly in these days, for the enemy is seeking to get in at some point to divert us from the “due order” (1 Chronicles 15: 13) of the will of God. We need to be sensitively alert to the influence of the blessed Spirit, maintaining communion, so as not to be afraid of God, and not miss the blessing of His presence.

Dear brethren, we need to be on our guard. We have been blessed of God in this city. We can speak experimentally, that we have had the sense that God is with us—we say it humbly, thankfully, worshipfully, that God is with us, and surely we want to be on our guard lest anything be allowed to cause God to have an issue with us. He had an issue with David, because he did not seek a current word from God for guidance in bringing up the ark. May we be refreshed by a conscious sense that God has spoken to us to the end that we may be wholly in accord with what is pleasurable to Him.

David, as recovered, saw to it that on the second occasion everything was done according to the “due order”. On the first occasion “David and all the house of Israel played before Jehovah on all manner of instruments”. That stresses variety. You might have thought that was a wonderful occasion, but the “due order” was lacking. There had been disregard of the divine command; there had been a turning aside from the truth. How could God prosper it? How could He bless it? There was much activity, but God was not in it and His hand was heavy upon David.

But now, this second time, David brought the ark “into the city of David with joy”. The ark was on priestly shoulders; sacrifice had entered into the occasion—“When they that bore the ark of Jehovah had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fatted beast. And David danced before Jehovah with all his might ... girded with a linen ephod”. David was in priestly attire; there was nothing—to displease the divine presence. Jehovah would consider this scene with great delight, free to pour out His blessing, and there was great joy—“David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of Jehovah with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet”.

I just had this simple impression, that we might walk in the conscious enjoyment of divine approval, in exercise, lest anything should be allowed by us that is not consistent with the divine presence and commandment, and thus give the enemy opportunity to get in to rob us of the blessedness of our liberty in the presence of God. What we allow in ourselves will have its reflection in the assembly. We want to keep a clean place, a holy place, maintaining all that is due to God according to the “due order”. May our hearts be fully in it, for His name’s sake.

I read these scriptures, beloved brethren, having been affected by the value of the assembly to divine Persons, and that we might be encouraged as contemplating it, that the assembly might mean more to us. In these scriptures we get some impression of the love of Christ for the assembly; the way that He has loved the assembly; the way that He has served the assembly; the way that He presently loves the assembly and is presently serving it.

I think we would have some sense, too, beloved brethren, of the value of the assembly to the blessed Spirit; the way that the Spirit is serving the assembly in view of her being prepared for that day of presentation to Christ. What a journey it has been, as with the Spirit. What a journey it is, what a journey it will yet be in view of the presentation of the assembly to the heavenly Man. Well may we say, like Rebecca, as we contemplate the love and service of the Spirit, “I will go”. May we be prepared to be submissive to the Spirit in His operations and service in relation to the assembly in view of that day of presentation. He providing the energy, the spring, so that when we see Christ we move spontaneously towards Him.

What I had primarily in mind was the love of Christ for the assembly. He has been spoken of as a connoisseur seeking beautiful pearls. What a service, Christ looking for beautiful pearls! It says, “Having found one pearl of great value, he went and sold all whatever he had and bought it”. Who can measure that, beloved brethren; what Christ had, what He was prepared to surrender, what He was prepared to sell, that He might have the assembly for Himself—one pearl of great value. I think we would be impressed as we realise in some little way what Christ had—“all whatever he had”. How much Christ, we may say, has surrendered that He might have the assembly for Himself. As it says in Ephesians 5: 25, “Christ also loved the assembly, and has delivered himself up for it”.

I just have this impression, beloved brethren, that Christ was looking for something. You think of Him looking, searching what pearls, beautiful pearls! But it says, “Having found one pearl …”. That could only refer to the assembly, and He sold all whatever He had that He might have it.

We have the impression in Matthew 16 as to what is completely outside of man’s mind. The natural man could never think of these things. Indeed in Matthew’s gospel and Luke’s gospel the Lord refers to what the Father has hid from the wise and prudent and revealed to babes.

Take the wisest man in this world—these things are completely outside his knowledge. It involves the Father’s revelation and also the service of the blessed Spirit to apprehend these great thoughts. The Lord says, “But ye, who do ye say that I am?”. Peter says, “Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God”. What a confession, beloved brethren! What an impression Peter had of this Man of whom he spoke. I believe, in some sense, he had it by experience, though he was to be formed in it still further through experience with Christ and his knowledge of Him. I believe he saw features in Christ that called out this confession. It was revealed to him by the Father. The Father’s sovereign operations were involved in revealing this to Peter; and yet I believe that he saw before him someone completely superior to every other man—“Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God”. Jesus says, “Thou art Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly”. What a confession by Peter! Christ has built on that.

Nothing will fail in the hands of Christ. What a Rock He is, beloved brethren. The assembly will be completely secure in the hands of Christ. Even the great administration of evil, hades’ gates, will not prevail against it. What a comfort for us in these days, that things are secure and safe in the hands of Christ.

I believe that the Lord’s word, “Thou art Peter, and on this rock I will build my assembly”, involves the rock-like character of the divine work in the saints that, as committed, will see the testimony through. There is what is secure and absolutely sure in the hands of Christ, but as the divine work is there in the saints things will be preserved. I believe that in “two of you” in Matthew 18: 19 there is what is of rock-like character that will maintain the testimony right to the end. In localities “two of you” assembly-minded persons—is what is required, beloved brethren, to maintain the testimony to the end. Think of the work of Christ, “On this rock I will build my assembly”. What the assembly means to Christ!—“My assembly”. And we have things worked out in Matthew 18, but worked out in all the preciousness of what the assembly is to Christ. I believe we will hold things rightly in our local settings, and value the assembly in its universal setting, as we appreciate what the assembly means to Christ—“My assembly”.

As to Ephesians 5 I am thinking not only of the way that Christ has loved the assembly—it says, “Christ also loved the assembly, and has delivered himself up for it”, and in some sense that would be historic—but of His present service—He is presently serving the assembly by the washing of water by the word. Even an occasion like this Christ would use to protect and preserve the assembly pure for Himself. It is not here to free it from sin; it is to maintain it fresh and pure for Himself. He will maintain the assembly in view of that day of presentation.

What a day that will be, beloved brethren! I think Christ longs for it, that day when he will have the assembly complete, glorious, without spot or wrinkle or any of such things. His own present, precious service is maintaining the assembly in this way with no spot or wrinkle or any of such things. Beloved brethren, we should appreciate the way that He has loved the assembly, but too the way that He is presently loving and serving it. He would use an occasion like this, He would use our reading meetings, He would use our occasions of fellowship together. He would use three-day occasions, in view of the assembly being maintained fresh and pure for Himself—His present, loving service to the assembly, the washing of water by the word. May we be affected by it.

Finally, we have that touching reference in Acts 20, where the beloved apostle is speaking to responsible persons in Ephesus. He is about to leave them, but he feels the need of a warning. He says, “Take heed therefore to yourselves”. I believe there is a need for this kind of self-judgment being maintained with us in view of a right outlook in relation to the assembly. We should maintain ourselves, beloved brethren, in relation to the truth, in view of the truth being maintained in our local gatherings. This will only be as first of all we take heed to ourselves.
Paul says, “Take heed therefore to yourselves, and to all the flock”. What a responsibility, and yet what a privilege, to have some little service in maintaining what is here for the heart of Christ!

Here it is God’s assembly. Indeed, I think in Scripture there is as much reference to the assembly of God, to the assembly in relation to God, as there is to it in relation to Christ, therefore we should value the assembly as the great vessel that stands related to God Himself, in view of praise, and in view of maintaining things here in testimony. Paul says, “to shepherd the assembly of God, which he has purchased with the blood of his own”. Think of the value to God of the assembly—“purchased with the blood of his own”. I think that is one of the most touching references in relation to the assembly. Well, Paul is using this as a lever.

He is using this to influence these elders in Ephesus, and it would come down to each one of us as having any sense of responsibility, that we might appreciate the assembly and devote ourselves in service to it. That involves the personnel. It is not an abstract thing; it involves maintaining principles, maintaining the truth, seeking to maintain persons in relation to the truth, in relation to principles. There is much on us, therefore, beloved brethren. The assembly as maintained here for Christ is the vessel which serves Him in praise, that delights His own heart as He comes into His garden. Think what the assembly means to Christ, “a garden enclosed ... a spring shut up, a fountain sealed” (Song of Songs 4: 12)—the assembly maintained wholly for Christ. How much it means to Him, beloved brethren! It is this vessel that Christ uses in the great service of praise, “To him be glory in the assembly in Christ Jesus unto all generations of the age of ages. Amen”, Ephesians 3: 21. Beloved brethren, we form part of that great and august vessel. May we appreciate what the assembly is to Christ and to God Himself, and commit ourselves in devotion to serve the assembly in view of things being preserved to the end. May it be so, for His name’s sake.

articles.title: THE LOVE OF CHRIST
articles.author: C. S. Elliott
articles.place: Word in meeting for ministry, Brooklyn, N.Y.

paragraphs.text: I am affected by the permanent character of love of the Lord Jesus. One can hardly find words, to express the character of love with which, as it says, Jesus “having loved his own who were in the world, loved them to the end”. The footnote says, ‘To the end’ does not give the full force, for it makes it refer to time; whereas going through with everything is implied.

It is a great support to one’s soul to know that we are loved by such a One. The apostle Paul could say, from experience, “The Son of God, who has loved me and given himself for me”, Galatians 2: 20. He knew the love of that Man. And we, in our measure, in our little part, know something of His love. The Lord Jesus, because of who He was; knew accurately what was going to happen to Him. He knew that the hour had come that He should depart out of this world to the Father; He knew the love of the Father’s heart; also, He knew what it was to be rejected; He knew what it would be to have all forsake Him. He could say to His disciples, earlier in this book, “Will ye also go away?”, John 6: 67. How the Lord Jesus feels things! He has the feelings of a Man, the affections of a Man. In chapter 11 it says, “Jesus wept”. He is affected by conditions which affect His own. At times we may feel downcast, but then the sense would come over us that there is One who loves us, as John put it here, “Having loved his own who were in the world, loved them to the end”. It is a love that carries right through! It taxes our love as to whether it is going through to the end. The love of the Lord Jesus went right through; no deviation, no diminution, in spite of what lay before Him.
It was love for your soul and mine, love for His God and Father, love for mankind, that led Him to go the whole way. But this word is that He loved His own and that He loved them to the end.

We are challenged as to our link with such a One who did not spare Himself but gave Himself so freely. There was no reserve on the part of the Lord Jesus. He saw the disciples through all that came upon them—there was Peter’s denial of Him; the fishing expedition in John 21, and the unbelief of Thomas—He sees us through all our trials and failures, giving us the sense of “the love of the Christ which surpasses knowledge”, Ephesians 3: 19. We have the sense that the love of Christ is just holding us up, and we get encouragement and strength to go through what lies ahead. Many are passing through pressures of one kind and another; many in bodily weakness, many getting old, with pressures in their bodies, but our spirits are refreshed with the knowledge that the love of
Christ is behind all—“Having loved his own who were in the world, loved them to the end”.

We would be affected by this—we know that our love is so feeble and so frail, and we are so changeable, but here we are in touch with a love which never deviates; a love that went right through and will be with us to the end. We are reminded that “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, and today, and to the ages to come”, Hebrews 13: 8. What a Man He is! The effect of having to do with Him should enter into our souls more, and energize us more, for the enemy is increasingly active. He seeks to rob us of what we have in our souls; he takes no holidays. But the love of Christ is active on our behalf and, as we have said, His love goes right through. We would therefore desire that our love for Christ should be sustained, and He is able to preserve us and keep our love for Him fresh and vital and living.

This has made a very real impression on me, for you look around and see things falling apart; standards are falling; things that we esteemed in years gone by have broken down; things are just falling apart in the hands of men, but when you think of the permanence of what is linked with Christ you realise that with Him there is no breakdown. May our souls get into that area with that Man with whom there is no breakdown or variation or shadow of turning! What a blessed thing! With Him there is that which is going through for the pleasure of the heart of God, and there is that which sustains us through all the circumstances through which we are passing. He could say, “I am with you all the days, until the completion of the age”, Matthew 28: 20. It is the love of this Man which is behind us, who “Having loved his own who were in the world, loved them to the end”.

Let us be faithful to Him. As we seek to be faithful to Him. He will see us through. His hand is not shortened. We may think that it is, because of our impatience and lack of faith. But His hand is not shortened; He has all the resources, all the reserves at His disposal; we just need to realise it more, that this is the Man with whom we are linked—the Lord Jesus Christ! May we draw on His help, for His name’s sake.

The eternal power and divinity of God are demonstrated, it is true, in the things that are made, but God speaks about His being almighty at a subsequent date to that of the creation. Now what I would say is that you do not require to compass almightiness; it is not necessary, but the knowledge that it exists in God is the solution to all difficulties that may arise from obstacles which appear in your way, and from obstacles which might seem to prevent the accomplishment of divine counsels. The comfort that lies in the almightiness of God is that there is no power that can stand in His way. It is a wonderful thing, as I said, to know that God is almighty, and every believer needs to know it. It is a fundamental element of the knowledge of God. If He is not almighty, there is a possibility of defeat; but if God is almighty there is no possibility of defeat in the heavens or in the earth. Knowing this, the christian is at perfect rest, for he, thereby, is in the secret that God, has ability to bring to pass all His pleasure.

“THEY SHALL COMFORT YOU” Ezekiel 14 speaks of Jehovah’s ways in judgment because of the sin of Israel, but the chapter concludes, “But behold, there shall be left in it those that escape, who shall be brought out of it, sons and daughters ... and ye shall see their way and their doings; and ye shall be comforted … And they shall comfort you”. One of the greatest privileges open to us is to seek to be a comfort to the people of God. There have been times of great pressure and humiliation, but what is to come out of them? May it be sons and daughters whose ways and doings bring comfort and joy to the saints! We have the Holy Spirit, one of whose titles is Comforter. He would fully furnish us to render service of that kind to one another.

EACH IN HIS ORBIT An interesting event occurred early this year when one of the smallest planets in the solar system came unusually near to the earth. It is a piece of rock about ten miles long—just a speck compared with some of the vast orbs in the heavens. But it has its own

orbit around the sun, and its, position at any moment can be exactly calculated. Is this not a picture of the spiritual system? We may think ourselves so small, so insignificant, but each believer has his direct link with Christ the Centre. Each is to be governed in his movements by the constraining power of the love of Christ (see 2 Corinthians 5; 14, 15) and by the principles which He has taught us. Thus we shall be in harmony with those who are truly subject to Him. Let us allow no wrong principle or influence to draw us out of our true and safe orbit in relation to our Lord Jesus Christ.
